1IVP.remarks: Early HIV-2 PR structure, closed-flap conformation

3EBZ.remarks: High-resolution DRV complex, key for understanding DRV resistance

3S45.remarks: APV/FPV binding mode in HIV-2 PR

Active Site.description: Contains the catalytic Asp-Thr-Gly triad; directly contacts inhibitor P1/P1' sites

Flap Region.description: Flexible beta-hairpin flaps that open/close to allow substrate entry

Flap Tip.function: Tip of the flap closing over active site
Flap Tip.description: Directly contacts bound drug; I50 is critical in HIV-2

Substrate Envelope.description: Positions lining the S1/S2/S1'/S2' subsites; mutations here affect drug vs substrate selectivity

Dimer Interface.description: Terminal residues that form the dimer interface; critical for PR assembly

Distal/Allosteric.function: Indirect modulation of active site geometry
Distal/Allosteric.description: Positions far from drug binding that can alter dynamics or stability

Flexibility Loop.function: Flexible surface loop connecting secondary structures
Flexibility Loop.description: High B-factor region; connects flap to core; variable in HIV-2

Hydrophobic Core.function: Structural stability; packing of helices and sheets
Hydrophobic Core.description: Conserved hydrophobic core; mutations here destabilize the fold

D30N.mechanism: Disrupts H-bond to NFV P2 amide

V32I.mechanism: Alters S1 subsite shape; hydrophobic expansion

I47V.mechanism: Reduces DRV binding affinity at flap

I50L.mechanism: Expands S2 subsite, preferential ATV resistance

I53V.mechanism: Reduces flap rigidity, lowers drug binding

V82A.mechanism: Reduces S1 pocket volume, excludes bulky P1 groups

N88S.mechanism: Hydroxyl-containing sidechain at NFV binding site

L90M.mechanism: Allosteric; alters S1/S1' pocket via beta-sheet repositioning

L10F.mechanism: N-terminal packing affects overall PR stability

G48V.mechanism: Restrains flap tip flexibility, reduces SQV binding

G73S.mechanism: Introduces polar group in surface loop

L76V.mechanism: Alters surface topology near dimer interface

key_interactions.detail: Flap I50 backbone NH -> drug P2/P1' carbonyl; D25 Odelta -> drug P1 NH
S1 pocket (V32, V82); S2 pocket (I54); flap contacts (I50)
Structural water bridging flap tip to inhibitor

mutations_disrupting.I50V: Alters flap H-bond pattern; moderate resistance
mutations_disrupting.I50L: Preferential ATV escape; expands active site

ATV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: HIV-2 PR has I32 (vs V32 in HIV-1), changing S1 pocket hydrophobicity. ATV retains activity in HIV-2 due to better S1 complementarity.

key_interactions.detail: D25, D30 backbone NHs; S53 backbone; bis-THF oxygens -> Asp backbone
Conserved water molecule network at flap-core interface

mutations_disrupting.V32I: Expands S1 pocket, reduces DRV complementarity

DRV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: DRV was co-crystallized with HIV-2 PR (3EBZ). Key difference: I32 in HIV-2 vs V32 in HIV-1 alters S1 pocket. DRV's bis-THF group compensates through backbone H-bonds.

key_interactions.detail: D25 Odelta; flap backbone; tetrahydrofuranyl oxygen network

FPV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: FPV shares amprenavir scaffold. I50V in HIV-2 is primary resistance; S1 pocket differences between HIV-1/2 partially explain cross-reactivity.

key_interactions.detail: Classic D25/D27 catalytic H-bonds; flap I50 backbone

IDV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: IDV is less effective in HIV-2 due to natural I32 and I50 positions. HIV-2 PR has inherently higher IDV resistance thresholds.

key_interactions.detail: D25 aspartate; flap backbone; P2 pyrimidinyl oxygen
Extensive van der Waals across all subsites

LPV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: LPV has the broadest cross-resistance profile in HIV-2. V47A and L76V are HIV-2-specific mutations not commonly seen in HIV-1.

key_interactions.detail: Standard aspartyl protease H-bonds; quinoline N -> flap backbone
Naphthyl in S1 (V82); P2 tert-butyl in S2

mutations_disrupting.G48V: Primary SQV resistance — restricts flap opening
mutations_disrupting.L90M: Major resistance mutation — allosteric S1 reshaping

SQV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: SQV was the first PI; L90M is a hallmark SQV resistance mutation conserved across HIV-1/2. G48V specifically impacts SQV's quinoline access.

key_interactions.detail: Coumarin carbonyl -> D25; pyridyl N -> backbone NH
Coumarin ring in S1/S1'; ethyl in S2
Aromatic contacts with flap and S1 pocket

TPV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: TPV has a unique non-peptidic scaffold. Less data available for HIV-2; I50V is predicted as primary resistance based on structural overlap.

key_interactions.detail: Standard catalytic H-bonds; D30 N -> NFV P2 amide (unique)

mutations_disrupting.D30N: Hallmark NFV resistance — eliminates unique D30 interaction

NFV/r.hiv1_vs_hiv2: D30N is NFV-specific across HIV-1/2. N88S is HIV-2-enriched (vs N88D in HIV-1), reflecting subtle S2' subsite differences.

23.note: HIV-2 has Leu — altered core packing

32.note: HIV-2 has Ile — smaller S1 pocket; critical for PI binding differences

47.note: Conserved flap residue; V47A is HIV-2-specific resistance

53.note: Flap core; I53V alters flap stability

54.note: S2 pocket; I54M/V common in HIV-2

88.note: NFV P2' contact; N88D/S NFV resistance

90.note: S1 reshaping; L90M major SQV resistance

47.hiv2: I (WT same), V47A is HIV-2-specific resistance

76.hiv2: L (WT same), L76V is HIV-2-specific resistance

82.hiv2: V (WT same), V82 mutations affect S1 pocket

resistance_hypotheses.rationale: Position 1 (P) is at the dimer interface (region: Dimer Interface) with importance 0.6155. HIV-2 protease is active only as a homodimer. Mutations at the dimer interface could destabilize the active dimer, raising the effective concentration needed for drug inhibition. This could manifest as apparent resistance through reduced PR activity rather than altered drug binding. Conservation: 0.98.
resistance_hypotheses.experimental_prediction: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) or analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) to measure dimer/monomer equilibrium for {wt}{pos}X variants. Determine dimer dissociation constant (Kd). Viral fitness assays expected to show reduced replication due to impaired PR assembly.

resistance_hypotheses.rationale: Position 6 (W) is in the hydrophobic core (region: Hydrophobic Core) with importance 0.0799. The core maintains the overall fold of the protease. Mutations here could alter the conformational ensemble, shifting the equilibrium between active and inactive states. Even small changes in core packing can propagate to the active site through correlated motions in the protein matrix. Conservation: 0.98.
resistance_hypotheses.experimental_prediction: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) or circular dichroism (CD) to measure thermal stability. Molecular dynamics simulations to assess conformational changes. X-ray crystallography to detect subtle structural rearrangements at the active site.

resistance_hypotheses.rationale: Position 11 (V) is distal from the active site (region: Distal/Allosteric) with importance 0.0164. Allosteric communication pathways connect distal positions to the active site through correlated motions. Mutations here may propagate structural changes through the protein matrix.
resistance_hypotheses.experimental_prediction: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) comparing WT vs {wt}{pos}X variants. Expect altered exchange rates at the active site despite the mutation being distal. NMR relaxation dispersion may also detect changes in millisecond dynamics.

resistance_hypotheses.rationale: Position 7 (Q) has high ML importance (0.0159) in region 'Uncharacterized' but is not a known resistance mutation. Its structural role requires further investigation. Conservation: 0.84.
resistance_hypotheses.experimental_prediction: X-ray crystallography of {wt}{pos}X HIV-2 PR variants. Phenotypic resistance testing and viral fitness assessment.
